decisions.reason: Product A closely builds on the firm's existing baking knowledge and production capabilities, so the firm can readily interpret early results and improve it, making a drop very unlikely.

Product B extends the firm's existing tour and hospitality operations into a historic mill tour, but it is less directly tied to core baking knowledge, so the firm has moderate absorptive capacity and a somewhat higher chance of dropping it.
Product C is a sweet pastry that fits the firm's traditional confectionery skills and recipes, enabling the firm to learn from early results and continue improving it.
